title: A Postcard for the Bakery
premise: Mirabel Ravensworth keeps her grandfather's lighthouse on the Cornish coast and writes novels under a name no one in the village knows. When a snowstorm traps her with Callum Vane—the rival novelist she loved and lost in London a decade ago—she must decide whether the identity she's hidden behind can survive being truly seen. As the festival approaches and the last train becomes a symbol of everything she's ever run from, Mirabel and Callum choose to stay, ending with them publishing a joint book and lighting the lighthouse together.
about_author: Quentin Thackeray is the pseudonym of a former coastal archivist who spent years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction. They live in a converted signal station and insist all first drafts be written during storms.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She maintains the lighthouse, hides her bestselling novels from the village, and counts the days until the winter festival. When she learns a famous author is coming to speak, she shrugs it off. Emotional beat: the comfort and quiet loneliness of a carefully curated invisibility.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the 4:10
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He arrives in the village incognito to research a novel about lighthouses, resentful of his publisher's demands. He doesn't recognize the woman who sells him a meat pie until he sees her handwriting on a chalkboard. Emotional beat: recognition as a small, terrifying jolt.

chapters.title: What the Storm Closed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The snowstorm hits early; roads close, the last train is cancelled, and Callum is stranded at the lighthouse. Forced proximity resurrects a decade of unsaid things, including the manuscript they once wrote together and burned. Emotional beat: old wounds reopening under warm light.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Page
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She discovers Callum has been reading her secret novels, recognizing her voice. He confronts her gently; she denies everything, then can't sustain the lie. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being truly known after years of pen names.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee Objects
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Village life intrudes: the festival committee needs a headline speaker, and Callum is drafted. Mirabel watches him charm the village she loves, feeling both pride and possessive fear. Emotional beat: jealousy of a world that gets to claim him openly.

chapters.title: Letters We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She finds her grandfather's old letters revealing he too once abandoned a love for duty at the light. She and Callum argue about sacrifice—whether staying is devotion or cowardice. Emotional beat: the generational echo that reframes her fears.

chapters.title: The Rival's Draft
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He reads Mirabel's unpublished manuscript and realizes it's their story—her version of their decade apart. Humiliated and moved, he writes his own ending and leaves it on her desk. Emotional beat: rivalry transmuted into collaboration.

chapters.title: Last Train Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm breaks; a train will run once, before the festival. Callum's publisher demands his return. At the platform, Mirabel tells him to go—protecting her secret one last time—and immediately regrets the shape of her own courage. Emotional beat: the lowest moment, self-sabotage in the name of duty.

chapters.title: The Light She Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. During the festival, the lighthouse fails in a final squall, and Mirabel, climbing to fix it, is nearly lost. Callum, who never boarded the train, helps her relight it in front of the whole village—her identity as the famous novelist exposed in the beam. Emotional beat: visibility chosen by crisis, love proven by staying.

chapters.title: A Postcard for the Bakery
chapters.summary: Callum's POV, resolution. Weeks later, they co-author a book under both names; the village claims them both. Callum mails a postcard to the bakery where they first met, announcing they're staying through spring—and longer. Emotional beat: belonging as a decision renewed daily, the lighthouse lit behind them.
